question: What the four windows a unit is ordered from show and post - the division designer and its brigade picker, the ship, air and brigade builders - with the command the ship builder posts, what refuses an order, and how a new unit is named.

addresses.name: CDivisionDesigner::CDivisionDesigner
addresses.no_signature: three stack arguments and a returned `this`; the two after `this` are the game screen and the window's name, and their types were not settled
addresses.comment: The constructor. Makes the window by the name it is handed (`division_designer`), sets parallel (+0x150) and serial (+0x154) to 1 and the template on show (+0x184) to -1, and attaches eight observers by element name: `accept`, `cancel`, `parallel_minus`, `parallell_plus`, `serial_minus`, `serial_plus`, `save_template` and the checkbox `as_reserves`. For each template of the country (CCountry +0x148) the button `divdesign_button` + n gets one shared handler, the text of the template's name and its index as text. Last it makes the CBrigadePicker (`brigade_picker`, +0x1C4) and calls its own slot 4. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: The decompiled C: `param_1[0x54] = 1; param_1[0x55] = 1; param_1[0x61] = 0xffffffff`; the seven `std::string::assign` of the names each followed by slot 13 of the window and the observer at slot 1 of the element's +0x48; `operatorPlusChars("divdesign_button", itoa(i + 1))`; `operator_new(0x74)` and `"brigade_picker"`.

addresses.name: CDivisionDesigner::Rebuild
addresses.comment: Slot 0: hides the window (slot 3), destroys it, makes it again by the name it had and re-attaches `accept` and `cancel`. Returns 1.
addresses.evidence: The decompiled C: slot 3 of `this`, slot 20 of the window, the game screen's slot 14 to get the factory and its slot 11 to make the window, then the two names.

addresses.name: CDivisionDesigner::Show
addresses.comment: Slot 2: works the design out (UpdateDesign), shows the window and tail-jumps to the brigade picker's slot 2, which populates its list.
addresses.evidence: The decompiled C: `FUN_007e6160(this)`, slot 13 of the window's CGuiObject, slot 11 of the window, then `[this+0x1C4]` slot 2.

addresses.name: CDivisionDesigner::Hide
addresses.comment: Slot 3: hides the window and tail-jumps to the brigade picker's slot 3.
addresses.evidence: The decompiled C: slot 14 of the window's CGuiObject, then `[this+0x1C4]` slot 3.

addresses.name: CDivisionDesigner::Update
addresses.comment: **Slot 4: the window's own controls, every frame it is open.** Floors parallel and serial at 1. `save_template` is shown only while a template is on show (+0x184 >= 0). Each `divdesign_button` + n takes frame 2 when it is that one and 1 otherwise. `brigade_queue` is rebuilt when its length differs from the design's (+0x1BC). `accept` takes the text of START_PRODUCTION and is enabled, then disabled again unless CanBuildDivision answers yes for serial * parallel divisions, or when the country's manpower (+0xBCC) is under the cost at +0x1C8. `total_sof` is set to frame 1. `paralell_value` and `serial_value` are the two counts; a minus button is disabled under 2 and a plus button at 99. In custom game mode `accept` says BUILD, the serial pair is hidden and `paralell_label` becomes DIVISIONS_TO_BUILD. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: `cmp dword ptr [esi+0x184],ebx; jge` choosing slot 14 or slot 13 of `save_template` (0x7E4F56); the loop to 0x7E5125 with `push 2` / `push 1` before slot 18; `cmp eax,edi; setne` on the list's count against `[esi+0x1bc]` (0x7E5174); `call 0x4e1190` with `[+0x154] * [+0x150]`; the four `< 2` and `< 99` tests in the decompiled C.

addresses.name: CDivisionDesigner::UpdateDesign
addresses.comment: **Works the design out and writes every figure of it.** `ret 4`, the designer on the stack. Per brigade of the list at +0x1B4: a CRegiment of the type with every technology at the country's level (CTechnologyStatus +0x218), ApplyTechnologies, and a copy of its definition. **Sums**: max_strength, width, soft, hard and air attack, defensiveness, toughness, air defence, suppression, supply and fuel consumption. **Averages**: max_organisation and softness (+0x1D0), and every adjuster - `sum * 1000 / (count * 1000)`. **The least**: max_speed. **The greatest**: piercing_attack and armor. Manpower (+0x1C8) is the sum of CCountry::GetBuildCostManpower with the `as_reserves` checkbox; days the greatest GetBuildTime * 1000; IC a day (+0x1CC) the sum of `GetBuildCostIC * days / 1000`, times 1000 over the greatest days - RecalculateCost's arithmetic. Shown: `ic_cost_value` times parallel and `mp_cost_value` times serial * parallel, two decimals; `build_time_value` days times serial as `N DAYS` up to 365 and `N / 30 MONTHS` above. The combined arms indicators, the terrain tooltip text (+0x1D4), the `on_complete_box` entries and the traffic light - green when `GetICPart(production) - GetUsedIC() - cost >= 0`, orange when the first two leave anything, red otherwise - are all here too. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: The accumulators 0x7E6BFC..0x7E6D4E: `mov eax,[esi+0xec]; add [esp+0x38],eax` and so on through +0xE8, +0xF0, +0x134, +0x138, +0x140, +0x11C, +0x128, +0x120, +0x124, +0x130, +0x110, +0x114; `cmp [esi+0x108],eax; jge` for the least; `cmp eax,ecx; jle` on +0x13C and +0x12C for the greatest. `call 0x4e1880`, `call 0x4e19a0; imul eax,eax,0x3e8`, `call 0x4e18f0; imul [esp+0x20]; ... call __alldiv` (0x7E7145). `cmp edi,0x16d; jle` before DAYS and MONTHS. `call 0x503d10` with `push 2`, `call 0x4f4b60`, `sub edx,eax; ... sub eax,ecx; js` at 0x7EA6C5.

addresses.name: CDivisionDesigner::BuildTooltip
addresses.no_signature: not read; the sibling CProductionView::BuildTooltip takes an out string and one more argument
addresses.comment: Slot 6: the tooltip builder. Forty-odd arms, each an element name against a pair of keys - `sort_str` / `total_str` with BUILD_STR_IRO and BUILD_STR_DRO, and so on for every column, the four order buttons with BUILD_ADD_REM_BUNDLE, `terrainbonus` with the text UpdateDesign left at +0x1D4 and the `combined_arms_indicator_` icons with a key + `_desc`. Only its strings were read. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: The literals in its body in order, from a walk of it; no instruction was read.

addresses.name: CDivisionDesigner::OnAccept
addresses.comment: **The handler behind `accept`: orders the design.** `parallel` (+0x150) times it makes a CConstructUnitCommand (0x84 bytes) with the list at +0x1B4, the capital of the country played, `serial` (+0x154) as the amount and the state of the `as_reserves` checkbox, and hands it to the command queue; then CloseBuilderWindow. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: The decompiled C: the loop to `param_1[0x54]`, `operator_new(0x84)`, `CConstructUnitCommand(cmd, this + 0x1B4, capital_province_id, param_1[0x55], ..., checkbox->+0x60 == 1, player tag, ...)`, slot 6 of the object at the game screen's slot 18 +0x38, and `FUN_007d9890(this)`.

addresses.name: CloseBuilderWindow
addresses.comment: What `cancel` and a finished `accept` do in all four builder windows: the window's own slot 3 (hide), and the in-game screen's slot 37 with 1. In custom game mode it calls 0x665220 instead of the screen. The receiver is whichever of CDivisionDesigner, CShipBuilder, CAirBuilder and CBrigadeBuilder owns the button, so it is recorded as a free function. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Stored as the `cancel` handler by three constructors (0x7CF7A6, 0x7D7AC6, 0x7E3A5B) and called at the end of each accept handler; the decompiled C for the body.

addresses.name: CDivisionDesigner::AddBrigade
addresses.no_signature: the receiver arrives in ESI and the type on the stack
addresses.comment: **Adds a unit type to the design if there is room.** The designer in ESI, the type on the stack. Room is `count (+0x1BC) < (BRIGADES_IN_DIVISION + CTechnologyStatus +0x1C) / 1000`. Then the insert at 0x7EFB70, RebuildBrigadeQueue and UpdateDesign. Called by CPossibleBrigadeEntry's click (0x7EFA40). Ghidra's RTTI pass had labelled this address a CPrioComparator constructor; it is not one. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: `mov eax,[esi+0x1bc]`; GetDefines, `[eax+0xac]` then `+0x80`, plus `[technology status + 0x1c]`, the divide by 1000 as a multiply by 0x10624DD3, and the compare; `call 0x7efb70`, `call 0x7e4d60`, `call 0x7e6160`. The caller: `mov esi,[eax+0x28]; push ecx; call 0x7ea880; pop esi` at 0x7EFA4B.

addresses.name: CDivisionDesigner::RebuildBrigadeQueue
addresses.comment: Empties the list `brigade_queue` and adds one CSelectedBrigadeEntry (0x88 bytes) for each type of the design. The designer on the stack. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: The decompiled C: `"brigade_queue"`, slot 31 of the window, slot 23 of the list, then the walk of +0x1B4 with `operator_new(0x88)` and slot 4 of the list. The caller pushes the designer and does not clean up (0x7E51A0).

addresses.name: CDivisionDesigner::OnTemplateButton
addresses.comment: The handler every `divdesign_button` shares: reads the index the constructor stored in the button as text (`atoi` of the string at its +0x08) and, when it is under 12, empties the design and calls LoadTemplate. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: The decompiled C: `atoi(button + 8)`, `uVar1 < 0xc`, `CList_FreeAndClear(this + 0x1B4)`, `FUN_007e45b0(index)`.

addresses.name: CDivisionDesigner::LoadTemplate
addresses.no_signature: the receiver arrives in EDI and the index on the stack
addresses.comment: Copies a template of the country's into the design: walks the CList at the template's +0x24 (the template being `[CCountry +0x148][index]`) appending each type to +0x1B4, sets the template on show (+0x184), and calls RebuildBrigadeQueue and UpdateDesign. The designer in EDI, the index on the stack. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: The decompiled C: `[[country + 0x148] + index * 4] + 0x24`, the inlined list append on +0x1B4 / +0x1B8 / +0x1BC, `*(this + 0x184) = index`.

addresses.name: CDivisionDesigner::OnSaveTemplate
addresses.comment: The handler behind `save_template`. With a template on show (+0x184 >= 0) it builds a template object (0x34 bytes) out of the country's own at that index, replaces its list with the design, and posts a CChangeTemplateCommand (0x7C bytes) for (the country, the index, the template). Ghidra's RTTI pass had labelled this address a CDivisionTemplate constructor. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: The decompiled C: `-1 < param_1[0x61]`, `operator_new(0x34)`, `FUN_0057ef20([country + 0x148][index])`, the walk of `param_1[0x6d]`, `operator_new(0x7c)` and `CChangeTemplateCommand(...)`. Stored at the designer's +0x190 by the constructor.

addresses.name: CDivisionDesigner::RepeatElapsed
addresses.no_signature: the receiver arrives in ESI; the answer is a bool in AL
addresses.comment: **The auto-repeat of the four order buttons.** The designer in ESI. If the timer at +0x1F0 is not running it is started and the answer is yes; otherwise the answer is yes, and the timer restarted, only when it has run longer than 0.1 s - or 0.3 s while the byte at +0x1F4 is set, which the press handler (0x7E4690) sets and this clears. The four hold handlers (0x7E4740, 0x7E4830, 0x7E4920, 0x7E4A20) act only when it says yes. CShipBuilder has the same at 0x809890 on +0x208 / +0x20C. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: The doubles at 0x160A410 (0.1) and 0x160A418 (0.3), chosen by `cmp byte ptr [esi+0x1f4],0`; slots 6, 1, 5 and 2 of the object at +0x1F0.

addresses.name: CDivisionDesigner::OnSerialPlusHeld
addresses.comment: The hold handler of `serial_plus`: when RepeatElapsed says yes, serial (+0x154) goes up by 1, or by 10 while the game screen's input object (its +0x1C) answers slot 12, and UpdateDesign is called. 0x7E4830 is the same on parallel (+0x150); 0x7E4920 and 0x7E4A20 take away, the ten-step one flooring at 1. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: The decompiled C of all four, which differ only in the offset and the sign.

addresses.name: CSelectedBrigadeEntry::CSelectedBrigadeEntry
addresses.no_signature: four stack arguments and a returned `this`; not typed
addresses.comment: The constructor of one line of the designer's `brigade_queue`: a `brigade_entry` window with `name` set to the type's name (its slot 6), `counter_type` given the sprite `GFX_counter_` + the type's key when there is one, `counter_size` set to frame 1, and `cancel` attached to 0x7EC900, which unlinks this type from the designer's list and calls UpdateDesign.
addresses.evidence: The decompiled C: `"brigade_entry"`, `"cancel"`, `"name"`, `"GFX_counter_"` + `param_3 + 2`, StringHashFind, `"counter_type"` slot 57, `"counter_size"` slot 18 with 1.

addresses.name: CBrigadePicker::CBrigadePicker
addresses.no_signature: four stack arguments and a returned `this`; not typed
addresses.comment: The constructor of the designer's second window, `brigade_picker`. Attaches one handler (OnSort) to twenty-one buttons - `sort_prio`, `sort_str`, `sort_sa`, `sort_ha`, `sort_piercing`, `sort_armored`, `sort_ad`, `sort_org`, `sort_cw`, `sort_aa`, `sort_def`, `sort_tou`, `sort_speed`, `sort_sup`, `sort_sc`, `sort_fc`, `sort_ic`, `sort_mp`, `sort_time`, `sort_sof`, `sort_off` - and starts with a CPrioComparator whose byte is clear at +0x70: priority, largest first. +0x28 is the designer. Ghidra's RTTI pass had labelled this a CPrioComparator constructor.
addresses.evidence: `mov dword ptr [esi],0x15de120` (the class's vftable); the twenty-one names; `mov dword ptr [eax],0x15dd958` into the 8-byte object stored at +0x70 (0x7ED0D0), with `mov byte ptr [eax+4],0`.

addresses.name: CBrigadePicker::Populate
addresses.comment: **Fills the list of brigades a division may be designed from.** Empties `queue`; for every definition of the database in order, those with is_land (+0x2D) and is_buildable (+0x36) for which CCountry::CountMaxUnitsStillBuildable is 1 or more get their definition made at the country's levels (0x507500) and are inserted by the comparator at +0x70 (0x7EFB70); then one CPossibleBrigadeEntry is made for each in that order. The ship builder's 0x80F230 is the same body with is_ship. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: The decompiled C: `arg1->isRegiment != false && arg1->isBuildable != false`, `CountMaxUnitsStillBuildable(...)`, `-1 < iVar4 + -1`, `FUN_00507500`, `FUN_007efb70(&list, &definition, param_1[0x1c])`, then the walk making 0x88-byte entries.

addresses.name: CBrigadePicker::OnSort
addresses.comment: **One handler for all twenty-one sort buttons.** Frees the comparator at +0x70, compares the button's name against each `sort_*` in turn, makes that column's comparator (8 bytes: a vftable and a byte), gives it the column's own byte from +0x2C on, flips that byte, and calls Populate. So the first click on a column sorts largest first and the next smallest first. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: 0x7EDD87..0x7EDE12 for `sort_prio`: `call free` on `[esi+0x70]`, the inlined compare against 0x15DD0BC, `operator_new(8)`, `mov dword ptr [eax],0x15dd958`, `mov cl,[esi+0x2c]; mov [eax+4],cl; cmp byte ptr [esi+0x2c],bl; sete dl; mov [esi+0x2c],dl`, `call 0x7ed1f0`, `ret 4`; the next arm does the same with 0x15DD960 and +0x2D.

addresses.name: CList_InsertSorted
addresses.no_signature: three stack arguments; who cleans up was not read
addresses.comment: Inserts into a CList by a comparator: walks back from the last node while `comparator->slot0(node.data, new)` answers yes and links the new node after the first it answers no for, or at the front (0x45F5E0) when it never does. With a comparator that answers `a < b` the list comes out largest first, and equal ones keep the order they were inserted in. Three arguments: the list, a pointer to the item, the comparator. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: The decompiled C: `puVar3 = param_1[1]` (last), the loop on `(**param_3)(*puVar3, *param_2)` moving to `puVar3[1]` (previous), and the two link arms.

addresses.name: CPrioComparator::Compare
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CPrioComparator::Compare(CPrioComparator* this, CSubUnitDefinition* a, CSubUnitDefinition* b)
addresses.comment: The whole of a builder list's comparator: `a->priority < b->priority`, or `>` when the byte at this +0x04 is set. `ret 8`. Each of the other comparators is the same eleven instructions on its own field - CStrengthComparator (0x7D7710) on max_strength, CICCostComparator (0x7CF4B0) on BuildCostIC, the definition's own and not the country's price.
addresses.evidence: `cmp byte ptr [ecx+4],0; mov ecx,[eax+0x194]; jne; cmp ecx,[edx+0x194]; setl al; ret 8` and the other arm with `setg`.

addresses.name: CPossibleBrigadeEntry::CPossibleBrigadeEntry
addresses.no_signature: three stack arguments, `ret 0xC`, and a returned `this`; not typed
addresses.comment: **The constructor of one line of the brigade picker, which is where its columns are written.** A `brigade_entry_2` window. It makes a CRegiment of the type with every technology at the country's level, summing the levels, and from that definition writes `str` (max_strength * 100 through 0xAB7380), `org`, `cw`, `sa`, `ha`, `aa`, `piercing`, `armored`, `def`, `ad`, `tou`, `sup` and `off` with no decimals, `sof` as softness * 100 + `%`, `speed` through 0x5A54F0, `sc` and `fc` with two, `ic` as GetBuildCostIC(country, definition, levels, false) and `mp` as GetBuildCostManpower(country, definition, false) with two, and `time` as GetBuildTime(country, definition, levels) whole. CPossibleSingleBrigadeEntry's constructor (0x7DE3B0, `brigade_entry_3`) is the same length to the byte. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: 0x7EEB7A..0x7EF948: each element's name pushed, then `mov ecx,[edi+N]` with N = 0xF0, 0xE8, 0x134, 0x138, 0x140, 0x13C, 0x12C, 0x11C, 0x128, 0x120, 0x130, 0x110, 0x114, 0x118 and `push 0` or `push 2` before `call 0xa5aca0`; `push 0x186a0` and the divide by 1000 on +0xEC and +0x124; `call 0x4e18f0`, `call 0x4e1880`, `call 0x4e19a0; ... call 0xa5ab40`.

addresses.name: CPossibleBrigadeEntry::OnSelect
addresses.comment: The slot the class introduces: the click on `select`. Calls CDivisionDesigner::AddBrigade with the entry's type (+0x78) on the designer the picker (+0x7C) holds at its +0x28. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: `mov eax,[ecx+0x7c]; test eax,eax; je; mov ecx,[ecx+0x78]; push esi; mov esi,[eax+0x28]; push ecx; call 0x7ea880; pop esi; ret`.

addresses.name: CanBuildDivision
addresses.no_signature: the design, a bare CList, arrives in ECX with the country and the number of divisions on the stack; written __thiscall it would need a class the list does not have
addresses.comment: **What disables the designer's `accept`.** The design - a CList of unit types - in ECX. False when it holds more than `(BRIGADES_IN_DIVISION + CTechnologyStatus +0x1C) / 1000` brigades **or fewer than two**; false when any of them has is_buildable (+0x36) clear; false when, for any type n times in it, `CountMaxUnitsStillBuildable(country, type) - n * divisions` is under nothing. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: `mov eax,[ecx+8]` (the count); GetDefines, +0xAC, +0x80, plus `[[country+0xdf8]+0x1c]`, over 1000; `cmp eax,esi; jl` and `cmp [ecx+8],2; jl` to the false return (0x4E11BE..0x4E11D6); `cmp byte ptr [eax+0x36],0`; the map built with 0x474A30 and walked calling 0x4E13A0.

addresses.name: CCountry::CountMaxUnitsStillBuildable
addresses.comment: **How many more of a unit type the country may have.** The game's own name, out of the Lua API. 0 when the technology status's unit_available (+0x27C) has the type clear, when SubUnitDefinitionIsUsableBy says no, or when the type has an available_trigger that is false for the country. 1,000,000 when both minimum_of_type (+0x1B8) and max_percentage_of_type (+0x1BC) are under 1. Otherwise it counts the country's brigades of the type's branch and of the type itself - in its units, in every military line of the queue (by the line's size) and in units waiting to be placed - and answers the greater of `minimum_of_type - have` and `all * max_percentage_of_type / 1000 - have`, never under 0. Callers: the four builder lists, CanBuildDivision and CBrigadeBuilder::Update. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: The decompiled C; the three early returns and the 1000000 are plain there. The counting loops were not checked in the listing.

addresses.name: CCountry::MakeUnitName
addresses.no_signature: five stack arguments - the country, the out string, the first brigade's definition, the level and a theatre - and who cleans up was not read
addresses.comment: **A name for a new unit of a given level** (0 theatre, 1 army group, 2 army, 3 corps, 4 division, 5 navy, 6 air). For a division the country's list of names for the first brigade's type (CCountry +0xCAC, indexed by the definition's index, 0x10 an entry holding a vector of 0x1C-byte strings) is tried once round from the cursor at +0xCBC, the cursor left on the one taken; a name already in use (0xA86F70) is passed over. Failing that, n = 1, 2, 3 ... through the text of DIVISION_NAME (and THEATRE_NAME, ARMYGROUP_NAME, ARMY_NAME, CORPS_NAME, NAVY_NAME, AIR_NAME) with NUM = n, ORDER = the text of ST, ND, RD or TH (`n % 10` in TH ST ND RD TH..., with 11 to 13 sent to TH) and TYPE = the text of the type's key + `_short`, until one is free. A theatre's first name can be NAMED_THEATHRE with a province instead. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: The decompiled C: `param_4 == 4`, `param_3[9] * 0x10 + param_1[0x32b]`, `param_1[0x32f]`, the `/ 0x1c` counts, the switch on the level with its seven keys, `local_18 % 10` and `local_18 - 0xb < 3`, the four pointers 0x15C0AF4..0x15C0B00 (`TH`, `ST`, `ND`, `RD`).

addresses.name: CCountry::MakeSubUnitName
addresses.no_signature: five stack arguments; who cleans up was not read
addresses.comment: **A name for a new brigade, ship or wing.** A type that is not land (is_land, +0x2D, clear) is first tried against the country's list for it, as MakeUnitName does; a land brigade never is - the lists under brigade types name divisions. Then n = 1, 2, 3 ... through REGIMENT_NAME for a land brigade and SUBUNIT_NAME for the rest, with NUM, ORDER and TYPE as there (and HOME, a province's name, when one is given), until one is free. A result equal to the key itself, or empty, is returned as it is. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: The decompiled C: `*(char *)(param_3 + 0x2d) == 0` guarding the list walk on `param_1 + 0xcac` / `+ 0xcbc`; `"SUBUNIT_NAME"` and `"REGIMENT_NAME"`; the three inlined compares of the result before the in-use test.

addresses.name: RegisterUnitName
addresses.no_signature: two stack arguments; who cleans up was not read

CConstructUnitCommand::Execute calls it after each name it makes and CConstructSingleUnitCommand's constructor after its one. The first argument, a country, is not used. The name is ours.

addresses.name: CConstructSingleUnitCommand::CConstructSingleUnitCommand
addresses.no_signature: nine stack arguments and a returned `this`; not typed
addresses.comment: **The constructor, which is where a ship ordered from the ship builder gets its name and its numbers - on the machine of the player who clicked.** Mints the command's id and the unit's from the counter at 0x1A857F8, makes one CBrigadeConstructionDefinition (0x54 bytes) for the type with an id of its own, names it through CCountry::MakeSubUnitName and RegisterUnitName, and copies the list of levels it is handed into the definition's model (+0x44). Fields: +0x3C/+0x40 the country, +0x44 the province, +0x50/+0x54 the unit id, +0x58 the definition, +0x5C the amount, +0x68 the build-now byte. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md, section 4.

addresses.name: CConstructSingleUnitCommand::Execute

structs.name: CShipBuilder
structs.comment: The window a ship is chosen and ordered in, one of the seven dialogs CProductionView owns. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md, section 4.
structs.evidence: RTTI names the class; slot 0 (0x408D30) sits at 0x15DF2E4 and slot 4 (0x40AA10) reads the fields recorded here.

struct_fields.name: division_size
struct_fields.comment: thousandths; what the technology key `division_size` adds up to. The most brigades a division may have is `(BRIGADES_IN_DIVISION + this) / 1000`: CDivisionDesigner::AddBrigade (0x3EA880), CanBuildDivision (0xE1190) and the designer's `allowed_value`. One technology of the base game has the key, `superior_firepower`.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x5374F0 adds `[technology + 0x1c] * scale` into it; `add ecx,edx` with `[eax+0x80]` (BRIGADES_IN_DIVISION) at 0x7E772F and the divide by 1000 after.

struct_fields.name: templates
struct_fields.comment: Begin of a vector of the country's division templates, end at +0x14C; from `default_templates` in its file under common/countries. A template has its name - a localisation key - as a string at +0x08 and a CList of unit types at +0x24. CDivisionDesigner's constructor names one `divdesign_button` for each.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov edx,[eax+0x14c]; sub edx,[eax+0x148]` and the `>> 2` count in CDivisionDesigner::Update (0x7E4FEC); `[[country + 0x148] + index * 4] + 0x24` in LoadTemplate.

struct_fields.name: unit_names
struct_fields.comment: Begin of a vector indexed by a unit type's index (CSubUnitDefinition +0x24), 0x10 bytes an entry, each holding a vector of 0x1C-byte strings: the names `unit_names` in the country's file gives that type. A division is named from its first brigade's list; a ship or a wing from its own.
struct_fields.evidence: `piVar12 = param_3[9] * 0x10 + param_1[0x32b]` and `(piVar12[1] - *piVar12) / 0x1c` in CCountry::MakeUnitName; the same on `param_1 + 0xcac` in MakeSubUnitName.
